lisa_support: Hey team — customer (acme-med) reporting requests from their on‑prem VPC are landing in EU inference endpoints even though they pinned us-west. Seeing +350–600ms latency and intermittent 401s. Billing spike from retries. Any quick checks?

mike_infra: Do we have sample request ids or headers? Is traffic going through their private egress proxy or via peering?

lisa_support: It's going through their egress NAT/proxy. They pasted a small header capture: Host: api.redwood-hosted.com, X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.5 — but backend logs show src ip 34.112.10.9 (cloud NAT EU).

kevin_sre: That smells like SNAT at the customer's cloud NAT changing the source IP into an EU nat pool. Our smart-routing uses source IP geolocation/ASN to pick region, so if the NAT hands us an EU exit IP we'll route to EU. Can they share traceroute/tcpdump?

lisa_support: Their repro steps: 
1) curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
2) tcpdump on proxy shows src 10.0.0.5 -> dst our vip; server side sees src 34.112.10.9 -> dst 3.120.45.10
They attached trace: traceroute hops into cloud-nat-eu before leaving.

mike_infra: Quick confirmation: if source IP is replaced by a cloud NAT IP in an EU CIDR, routing will pick EU. Two short-term options: preserve source IP (SNAT exemption/hairpin) or force region via header.

lisa_support: They tried adding X-Redwood-Region: us-west and a single request obeyed but their internal proxy strips that header. Also they see 401s because auth service is rate-limiting by source ip; many retries from the nat pool look like one noisy client.

kevin_sre: Proposed fixes: 
- Ask customer to add SNAT exemption for our destination CIDR (so their host IP is visible). 
- Encourage private peering/advertise onprem prefix so source IP preserved. 
- Implement account-level region pinning on our side (route by org metadata instead of source IP).
Short-term we can canary a rule to honor X-Region-Override for this org.

deploy-bot: deploy accepted: canary routing-rule 'org-pin/2801' (honor X-Region-Override for org acme-med) queued -> deploying to 10% of infra.

anna_sales: Flagging as P1: customer sees production impact and billing spike. Need ETA.

kevin_sre: Canary will be live in ~2h. For immediate mitigation we recommended they configure SNAT exemption or toggle proxy to preserve the client source. I'll DM their cloud network engineer template and ip ranges to exempt.

lisa_support: Created ticket CS-7891, attached server logs and customer tcpdump. Repro snippet from their tcpdump: 
```
10:12:01 IP 10.0.0.5.51234 > 3.120.45.10.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:654, ack 1, win 229,...
# server sees: src=34.112.10.9:51234 -> dst=3.120.45.10:443
```

mike_infra: Also suggested temporary rate‑debounce on retries for that customer to curb billing while root cause is addressed — we can throttle by nat-pool ip as emergency measure.

lisa_support: Customer confirmed throttling reduced retries and costs for now. We'll follow up after canary completes. Adding follow-up items to CS-7891: 
- Cloud NAT exemption guide for common providers
- Peering checklist
- Account-level region pin rollout task

kevin_sre: I'll update once canary is healthy. If it fails we'll revert and push a different mitigation.

lisa_support: Thanks — passing ETA and next steps to customer. :thumbsup:
